claim: Rupiah spot closed at Rp18.046 per US$ on Mon 19 Oct 2026 (−19 pts, −0,11% from Rp18.027); JISDOR Rp18.050. Re-check with the 20 Oct morning quote before rendering (market opens 09:00 WIB; no 20 Oct quote existed when this was written).
BI announces its BI-Rate decision on Wed 21 Oct 2026 (RDG 20–21 Oct); the options are a hold at 5,75% or a hike to 6%

On 4 Jun 2026 the rupiah closed above Rp18.000 for the first time, at Rp18.049 (−0,46%), described as its weakest level ever. Earlier that morning it broke Rp18.000 intraday (open Rp18.003, ~Rp18.014–18.025).
The 2026 low so far is the 8 Jun close, about Rp18.170 (Bisnis/TradingView) to Rp18.188 (Kontan). Shown on the chart only; 19 Oct (18.046) is not a record.
1998 crisis: the rupiah peaked around Rp16.800 per US$ (June 1998, intraday)
Covid 2020: the rupiah closed at Rp16.575 per US$ on 23 Mar 2020 (a close; the intraday range was ~16.600–16.700), its weakest since 1998
In 1998 the rupiah lost more than 80% of its value (from around Rp2.500)

After the rupiah crossed Rp18.000, BI raised rates twice in 10 days: 9 Jun 2026 (weekly RDG) +25 bp to 5,50%; 18 Jun 2026 (RDG 17–18 Jun) +25 bp to 5,75%. (Earlier, 20 May: +50 bp to 5,25%; 100 bp in total May–June.)
BI has held the BI-Rate at 5,75% since July (July, August, September 2026 meetings)
Today's pressure comes from the MSCI proposal to downgrade Indonesia (Emerging → Standalone) and the Fed still being open to more tightening (FOMC 27–28 Oct)
FX reserves US$146,3 miliar at end-September 2026
September 2026 inflation 3,28% yoy, within BI's 2,5±1% target

Hold option at 5,75%: some economists, e.g. Irman Faiz (Danamon), expect a hold, with BI 'buying time' through non-rate tools (FX intervention). Only one named October hold source found; Liputan6/Bloomberg Technoz hold calls are from August, and the Kontan October articles could not be opened. Wording: 'sebagian ekonom, misalnya Danamon'.

Hike option: Bloomberg Economics projects +25 bp to 6%. Citi (via Reuters, in CNBC) calls a hike a pre-emptive step to stop foreign outflows from stocks spreading to the bond market; Citi gives no level.

Trade-off: a hike can make loans more expensive (BI's own estimate: a 25 bp hike trims growth by ~0,1%); a hold leaves the rupiah exposed if pressure continues (economists: room to hold is not unlimited)
